summary: inventory main: clean shutdown may exit with a non-nil consumer error (same select race as TKT-98)
description:
Deferred from TKT-98 (plan-review decision D2). `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:201-210` has the identical racing shutdown select that TKT-98 fixes in access: `consumerErr` (fed by `cons.Run(ctx)`, whose tail returns a `context.Canceled`-wrapped error) races `<-ctx.Done()`, so ~50% of clean SIGTERM shutdowns exit non-zero reporting the consumer's cancellation instead of the clean `srv.Shutdown` result.

Same defect, same cost profile as TKT-98: cosmetic under Compose (exit code ignored on stop), misleading to any orchestrator that reads a non-zero exit as a crash.

Fix: apply the pattern TKT-98 ships in `services/access/cmd/access/main.go` -- an `awaitShutdown` helper that classifies a consumer error as shutdown-caused (`ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`) and falls through to the graceful-shutdown block, plus a non-blocking drain of `consumerErr` in the signal branch so both ready branches reach the same answer. Copy the test shape too (`services/access/cmd/access/shutdown_test.go`): pre-fill both channels, loop ~200 iterations, assert one answer.

Explicitly NOT a shared-package extraction. TKT-98 D2: one 3-line predicate used twice does not justify a `shared/` abstraction; revisit only if a third service adopts the same lifecycle contract. Inventory carries its own copy.

Note: inventory has a single `consumerErr` producer (access has two), so the buffered-1 two-producer wrinkle TKT-98 left alone (D1) does not apply here.

### Conditions of Success

- [ ] A clean SIGTERM exits **0 deterministically** — the consumer's `context.Canceled` tail no longer races `ctx.Done()` to the return value.
- [ ] A **genuine** consumer failure (not shutdown-caused) still exits non-zero and is reported.
- [ ] A loop test (~200 iterations, both channels pre-filled) asserts one answer, mirroring `services/access/cmd/access/shutdown_test.go`.
- [ ] The helper stays in `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/` — no `shared/go` extraction (see the ADR-034 note in the readiness comment).
- [ ] `make check` green.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed by TKT-98's plan-review stage, not by its ai-review -- the twin was spotted while briefing the plan drafter, and `quality-practices.md` §2's incidental disposition (file it, don't just note it) applies the same at plan time as at review time. Code pointer: `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:201-210`, verified byte-identical in shape to the access select at TKT-98's claim commit `d812d05`.

Not started: needs shaping (COS + the 8-item DoR incl. the context-memo bake) before it can pass Gate 1. The reference implementation it should copy will exist on `main` once TKT-98 merges.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### DoR — 8/8. Shaped 2026-07-28. Was the weakest of the four; two real gaps closed.

**Gap 1 — no COS.** The description was prose only. Five conditions added above.

**Gap 2 — a stale approach, and the reason it was invisible.** The description says "explicitly
NOT a shared-package extraction", citing TKT-98's D2 decision. That predates **ADR-034**
(TKT-127), which created a shared durable-consumer lifecycle package whose stated dividing line
is *"this package owns when a consumer stops and what it says about it."* Read literally, a
helper that classifies a consumer error looks like it belongs there.

**Decision taken at shaping (owner call, delegated): keep the local copy.** `awaitShutdown`
lives in `cmd/`, and it does not decide *when a consumer stops* — it decides how **main**
interprets an error the consumer already returned, alongside `srv.Shutdown` and
`ListenAndServe`, neither of which is the shared package's business. ADR-034's own exclusion
list keeps "startup readiness gates" and disposition with the owning service for the same
reason. So TKT-98 D2 stands: 3 lines, twice, no abstraction — revisit at a third service.
This is exactly what the plan gate is for; Gate 2 can overturn it cheaply, before code exists.

`governingAdrs` was an empty array with no note — the omission `shaping.md` warns about, and the
one that would have let a planner reading only code copy the helper without ever seeing ADR-034.
Now baked: **ADR-017** (the termination guarantee the shutdown path must not swallow) and
**ADR-034**.

Code re-verified at HEAD: the racing select is live, now at
`services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:206-215` (the ticket cited 201-210 — drifted).

**Verdict: READY.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — and this run is **gateless by owner waiver**

**⚠ Process experiment: all four human gates are waived for TKT-121.** The repo owner
explicitly waived them for this run so the ticket goes Ready → Done in one continuous
autonomous pass. Recording it here so the board history shows this ticket never stopped for
a human.

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | already given (ticket was in `Ready`) |
| 2 — plan approval | human moves Planning → Building | **agent self-resolves** open decisions: take the plan-critique's recommendation; absent one, take the most reversible option. Every self-made call is recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews PR and squash-merges | **agent merges** after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules). Review-guide still posted on the PR first — it is the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates COS | **agent self-validates** each COS against test evidence on the merged code. |

Everything else in the skill applies unchanged — `config.models` routing with no substitutions,
cross-model review for both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green
before every push and after the merge, all marker comments, no AI attribution anywhere.

**Selection reason:** the ticket was the highest-readiness item in `Ready` (DoR 8/8, shaped
2026-07-28), it is a single-file fix with an already-merged reference implementation on `main`
(TKT-98, `services/access/cmd/access/main.go:305`), and its blocking dependency was that
reference existing — which it now does.

**Blocker check:** zero open blockers. Both links (`TKT-98`, `TKT-122`) are `relates`, not
`blocks`. TKT-98 is `Done`.

**Risk label:** none, deliberately. The ticket is small but it carries a live design question —
whether ADR-034 claims this helper — which the readiness comment resolved one way at shaping and
the plan stage may overturn. `risk:low` would have skipped the plan gate; the gate is exactly
where that call belongs. (Moot under the waiver, but the reasoning is on the record and Gate 2's
substitute must still answer the question.)

**Cross-model invariant checked:** `plan=gpt-5.6-sol` ≠ `planReview=main-agent`;
`implement=main-agent` ≠ `aiReview=gpt-5.6-sol`. Both pairs distinct.
